q: The Branner-Hubbard work on cubic polynomials (non-connected Julia sets) introduced tableaux and the 'wringing' deformation. Tableaux track the orbit of the critical points in the puzzle structure. When all tableau entries are:
opts: 'Escaping' (mapped outside all puzzle pieces after finitely many steps), the corresponding cubic has a Cantor Julia set
Preperiodic, the critical point is eventually periodic
exp: In Branner-Hubbard theory: if all critical point orbits eventually escape the puzzle pieces (the tableau is 'escaping'), the Julia set is a Cantor set (totally disconnected). This generalizes Mandelbrot/Douady-Hubbard: connected Julia set ↔ bounded critical orbit, but for cubics there are two critical points.
